chapters.1.lds: The lesson invites readers to bring difficult questions to God as Habakkuk does. Why does the announced rise of Chaldeans create a second complaint?
chapters.1.summary: Habakkuk asks how long he must cry for help and not be heard. He sees violence, and justice never wins. God answers that he is raising up the Chaldeans. They are a fierce nation that sweeps across the earth. Their own strength is their god. Habakkuk objects that God’s eyes are too pure to look on evil. He asks why God is silent while the wicked swallow the more righteous. The enemy catches people like fish in a net.
chapters.2.lds: The lesson connects the prophet’s watch with waiting for answers from God. Why do stones and beams testify against their owner?
chapters.2.summary: Habakkuk stands at his watch post to see what God will say. The LORD tells him to write the vision plainly on tablets. It awaits its time, and he must wait for it. The proud one is not upright, and the righteous will live by faith. The conquered nations will taunt their conqueror with five woes. He piled up what was not his and built his house on plunder. Idols are teachers of lies. The LORD is in his holy temple, and all the earth must be silent.
chapters.3.lds: The lesson studies rejoicing in God when material sources of security fail. Which losses remain when the speaker chooses to rejoice?
chapters.3.summary: Habakkuk prays and asks God to remember mercy in his anger. He recalls God coming from the south in glory. Mountains shook, and the sun and moon stood still. God went out to save his people and crush the wicked. Habakkuk’s body trembles as he waits for the day of trouble. The fig tree may not bud, and the fields may give no food. The flocks and herds may be gone. Yet he will rejoice in the LORD, who is his strength.
